scope.environmentPolicy: Tune anomaly gameplay effects only; do not tune weather or emission occurrence.

parameters.label: Human Enemy HP
parameters.description: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.rationale: How many bullets a human enemy can soak up before going down. Higher = longer, more ammo-hungry firefights; lower = enemies drop fast. Vanilla: Novice 1×, Stalker 1.2×, Veteran 1×, Master 1.5×. Pair it with WEAPON DAMAGE — together they set your time-to-kill.
parameters.interaction: WEAPON DAMAGE affects the same time-to-kill from the opposite side. Raising enemy health while lowering your weapon damage compounds the effect.

parameters.label: Enemy Gun Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.rationale: How much it hurts when a human enemy shoots you. Low values let you tank a burst; high values make every exposed second dangerous. Vanilla: Novice 0.17×, Stalker 0.85×, Veteran 1.02×, Master 1.35×. Mutant bites and explosions have their own settings.
parameters.interaction: HUMAN ENEMY HP sets how long enemies survive; this sets how dangerous their shots are. PEAK / MINIMUM HIT PROTECTION also soften sustained fire.

parameters.label: Explosion Damage
parameters.description: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.rationale: How deadly grenades and other blasts are — both yours and the enemy's. Raise it if you want grenades to feel lethal, lower it to survive the odd F1 at your feet. Vanilla: Novice 0.25×, Stalker and Veteran 1×, Master 1.2×.
parameters.interaction: Only the difficulty boost. Each explosive keeps its own base damage.

parameters.label: Grenades
parameters.description: How often a squad of human enemies may throw a grenade. Rate r divides the pause of the CombatSynchronizer group tokens ThrowGrenade, Special.ThrowGrenade (all enemy ranks) on the selected difficulty.

notes: Group token pauses decide how often anyone in the fight may start this action; Easy/Medium/Hard inherit the Default table, Master owns its own (CombatSynchronizerStalker).
The four full rank tables are written together with SPECIAL ABILITY RATE and the other tactics (one writer).

parameters.rationale: How often human enemies throw grenades at you. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran every 20–35 s per squad, Master every 10–17 s. Shorter pause on COMBAT MINUTE = they do it more often.
parameters.logic: Every enemy rank's pause changes together; which enemy acts still follows vanilla tactics.
parameters.interaction: Other tactics, ENEMY ACCURACY and HUMAN AWARENESS are independent. Enemy gun damage is in HUMAN ENEMY COMBAT.

parameters.rationale: How often human enemies pin you down with suppressive fire. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran every 15–25 s, Master every 7–12 s. Shorter pause on COMBAT MINUTE = they do it more often.

parameters.label: Enemy Accuracy
parameters.description: Scales how tightly human enemies group their shots: divides DispersionRadius of all 77 NPC weapon settings (75 base game, 2 DLC1).

notes: DispersionRadius is the NPC weapon's own bullet spread (e.g. AK74 300); the distance curve and the zombie addend are unchanged.
Not changed by the game's difficulty; 1× is vanilla on every difficulty.

parameters.rationale: How accurately human enemies shoot. Vanilla: 1×. 2× = half the spread, so more bullets find you at range; 0.5× = twice the spread. Damage per hit is ENEMY GUN DAMAGE.
parameters.logic: 2× halves the spread of every enemy gun; 0.5× doubles it. 1× keeps vanilla spread.
parameters.interaction: Independent of the tactics; ENEMY GUN DAMAGE sets how much each hit hurts.

parameters.label: Enemy Sight
parameters.description: Scales how far human enemies see: CentralVisionDistance (80 m) and PeripheralVisionDistance (25 m) of the DefaultNPC vision scanner. Maximum 2.5× = 200 m ahead / 62.5 m peripheral.

notes: Human NPCs use the DefaultNPC vision scanner (ObjPrototypes NPCBase); bosses and zombies inherit from it.
Light, distance and angle penalty curves are unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How far human enemies can spot you. Vanilla: 80 m straight ahead, 25 m at the edge of vision. 0.5× = sneak much closer; 1.5× = they notice you from further away. Maximum 2.5× = 200 m ahead, 62.5 m at the sides.
parameters.logic: Higher = they spot you from further away, ahead and to the side; darkness, flashlights and night vision still matter.
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Enemy Hearing
parameters.description: Scales how far human enemies hear sounds: every non-zero HearingDistance of the base hearing sensor (shots 46 m, steps 12 m, voice 30 m, reload 7.5 m, explosions 60 m …).

notes: Human NPCs use DefaultNPC, which inherits the base sensor; zombie humans follow where they do not override. Mutants have their own sensor (unchanged).

parameters.rationale: How far human enemies hear you. Vanilla: footsteps 12 m, gunshots 46 m. 0.5× = you can move and shoot closer unnoticed; 2× = every step gives you away.
parameters.logic: Every sound range scales together: footsteps, gunshots, reloads. Sounds enemies never hear stay silent.
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Enemy Memory
parameters.description: Scales how long human enemies keep hunting you after losing track: DefaultNPC threat freeze time (30 s) and SearchEnemy freeze (30 s) are multiplied, their per-second threat loss divided.

notes: Threat memory of human NPCs; BossNPC inherits it. Individual threat sources (ConfidenceDropToZeroTimeSeconds) are unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How long human enemies keep searching after they lose you. Vanilla: they hold their alert about 30 s. 2× = they hunt you twice as long; 0.5× = they give up quickly.
parameters.logic: Higher = they stay alert and keep searching longer; lower = they calm down sooner.
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Fog Visibility
parameters.description: Changes the Fogy weather VisibilityCoef in AISettings. This is the actual weather coefficient (0.70 vanilla), not a guaranteed NPC sight range. Other weather, hearing, flair and luminance are untouched.

notes: STALKER 2 2.1 GameData/AIGlobals.cfg: AISettings > WeatherSettings > [2] has WeatherSID = Fogy, VisibilityCoef = 0.7, HearingDistanceCoef = 0.7 and FlairCoef = 0.7.
Runtime behavior and affected AI agent classes are unverified: this is a global weather AI coefficient, not proven human-only.
Do not change the separate fog luminance value (0.6f), hearing or flair.

parameters.rationale: How well human enemies see through fog. Vanilla: 70% of their clear-weather sight. Lower = fog hides you better; 100% = fog gives you no cover. Real spotting range also depends on light and cover.
parameters.logic: Only fog changes; clear weather, rain, storms and night vision stay vanilla.
parameters.interaction: Separate from SIGHT, which sets how far they see in clear weather.

parameters.label: Rain Noise
parameters.description: How much light or regular rain masks sounds from AI. Higher noise means less enemy hearing.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 AIGlobals.cfg WeatherSettings 3/4 has Rainy and LightRainy HearingDistanceCoef = 0.7.
Global AI weather coefficient; effects and AI-class scope still need an in-game test.

parameters.rationale: How much rain covers your noise. Vanilla: 30% — in rain enemies hear you at 70% of the normal range. Higher = sneak closer while it pours; 0% = rain gives you no cover.
parameters.logic: Shown as how much of your noise the rain hides: 30% = enemies hear you at 70% of the normal range. Applies to rain and heavy rain.
parameters.interaction: Only active during light or regular rain; independent of general HEARING. Range 0–90% in 5% steps.

parameters.label: Thunder Noise
parameters.description: How much thunder masks sounds from AI. Higher noise means less enemy hearing.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 AIGlobals.cfg WeatherSettings 5 has Thundery HearingDistanceCoef = 0.6.
Global AI weather coefficient; effects and AI-class scope still need an in-game test.

parameters.rationale: How much a thunderstorm covers your noise. Vanilla: 40% — enemies hear you at 60% of the normal range. Higher = thunder hides your steps and shots better; 0% = no cover.
parameters.logic: Shown as how much of your noise a thunderstorm hides: 40% = enemies hear you at 60% of the normal range.
parameters.interaction: Only active during thunder; independent of general HEARING. Range 0–90% in 5% steps.

parameters.label: Weapon Damage
parameters.description: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.rationale: The damage your own guns deal on a normal body hit. Lower values mean more bullets per kill and more ammo burned. Vanilla: Novice 1.3×, Stalker 1×, Veteran and Master 0.75×. Headshots get an extra boost on top from HEADSHOT DAMAGE.
parameters.interaction: HEADSHOT DAMAGE multiplies headshots on top. HUMAN ENEMY HP also changes the time-to-kill.

parameters.label: Headshot Damage
parameters.description: Scales the damage multiplier applied to your headshots; 1× is normal and 2× doubles the configured headshot damage.
parameters.rationale: Extra punch for your headshots on top of normal weapon damage. 2× doubles the headshot bonus, rewarding careful aim over spraying. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran 1×, Master 2×.
parameters.logic: 1.0× = the normal headshot multiplier; 2.0× doubles it. It multiplies, it doesn't add a flat bonus.
parameters.interaction: WEAPON DAMAGE sets the base hit; this multiplies headshots on top, so raising both stacks up.

parameters.label: Weapon Jam Rate
parameters.description: Changes how often worn weapons jam.
parameters.rationale: How often worn guns jam on you. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran 1×, Master 1.5×. Higher = keeping your gun repaired matters much more; 0.5× halves jams. A gun in good condition still rarely jams.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with weapon condition and each gun's own jam behavior.

parameters.label: Mutant Hit Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.rationale: How hard mutants hit when they reach you — bites, claws and charges. Mutant toughness is set separately in the health cards. Vanilla: Novice 0.35×, Stalker 1×, Veteran 1.35×, Master 1.5×.
parameters.interaction: Only damage mutants deal to you. MUTANT HEALTH sets how much they can take.

parameters.label: Peak Hit Protection
parameters.description: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: The game quietly softens damage when many hits land at once, so you don't melt in a single burst. This is the strongest that safety net can get. Higher = more forgiving under heavy fire, lower = bursts hit closer to full damage. Vanilla: Novice 100%, Stalker 75%, Veteran 50%, Master 40%.
parameters.logic: Higher = more protection when many hits land at once; lower = bursts hurt more. It's protection strength, not a straight damage cut.
parameters.interaction: MINIMUM HIT PROTECTION sets the weakest end. Enemy gun damage is separate.

parameters.label: Minimum Hit Protection
parameters.description: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale: The weakest end of the same hidden safety net against rapid hits. Raising it keeps some protection even in long, sustained fights. Vanilla: Novice 100%, Stalker 33%, Veteran 15%, Master 12%. Works together with PEAK HIT PROTECTION.
parameters.logic: Higher = more protection even in long firefights; lower = sustained fire hurts more. It's protection strength, not a straight damage cut.
parameters.interaction: PEAK HIT PROTECTION sets the strongest end. Enemy gun damage is separate.

parameters.label: Healed Damage Still Counts
parameters.description: Controls whether damage remains in the repeated-hit protection tracker after you heal it.
parameters.rationale: Whether hits you already healed still count against your burst protection. Vanilla: Novice and Stalker OFF, Veteran and Master ON. ON = patching up mid-fight doesn't reset the safety net; OFF is more forgiving.
parameters.logic: OFF = Novice and Stalker behaviour, ON = Veteran and Master. Healing always restores HP; this only decides whether PEAK / MINIMUM HIT PROTECTION still counts the healed damage.
parameters.interaction: Works with PEAK HIT PROTECTION. Healing still restores HP even while past hits count.

parameters.label: Bloodsucker Health
parameters.description: Scales Bloodsucker-family HP with one multiplier. The radar shows the standard Bloodsucker HP; Mist Bloodsucker follows the same multiplier; the Ashy and prologue variants follow the same multiplier.

notes: Directly scales the authored MaxHP field in GameData/ObjPrototypes.cfg.
1× is vanilla.
This is not selected through DifficultyPrototypes.cfg; the same generated MaxHP applies regardless of the in-game difficulty.
The Bloodsucker family control applies the same multiplier to Bloodsucker (500 MaxHP) and MistBloodsucker (1000 MaxHP); the radar displays the standard Bloodsucker value only.

Variants with their own MaxHP follow the same multiplier: AshyBloodsucker, PrologueBloodsucker. Collar variants inherit from the base prototype; illusion clones (Bayun clone, Pseudodog phantoms) are not scaled.

parameters.rationale: How tough Bloodsuckers are — the invisible stalkers of the Zone. Includes the Mist, Ashy and prologue variants. Vanilla: 1× (500 HP). Higher values mean longer, scarier close-range fights; every other mutant has its own card.
parameters.interaction: Only Bloodsucker health. Other combat settings are separate.

parameters.label: Bayun Attack Rate
parameters.description: How often a Bayun can use its attacks: claw swipes, leaps, pounces and dodges. Rate r writes cooldown multiplier 1/r for each of these cooldowns of every Bayun variant on the selected difficulty.

notes: Native per-agent, per-tag cooldown multiplier list of the selected difficulty (vanilla: Master only, 0.5).
Base cooldowns are AbilityPrototypes TriggeredCooldowns (seconds); agent entries match exact prototype SIDs, so every variant of the family is listed.
Families and tags the game never lists on Master need an in-game check.

parameters.rationale: How often Bayuns use their attacks — claw swipes, leaps, pounces and dodges. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran 1×, Master 2×. Higher = less breathing room between them.

parameters.interaction: Only HP loss from radiation. RADIATION ACCUMULATION sets how fast it builds; recovery and Anti-Rad clear it.

parameters.logic: Higher = every bleed hurts more; lower = bleeding is gentler.
parameters.interaction: LOW / MEDIUM / SEVERE BLEEDING DAMAGE set the HP lost per stage; NATURAL BLEEDING RECOVERY and meds decide how fast it stops.

parameters.label: Natural Bleeding Recovery

parameters.label: Passive HP Regen

parameters.rationale: Slow healing over time without using anything. Vanilla: 0 — in vanilla you never heal just by waiting. Even a small value makes minor wounds close up on their own.
parameters.logic: 0 = vanilla, no passive healing; higher = you slowly heal over time.
parameters.interaction: REGEN DELAY decides when recovery can begin. Low-health recovery and medkits stay separate.

parameters.label: Regen Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla player VitalParams define RegenHPDelayTimeSeconds = 5.

parameters.rationale: How long after taking damage your health starts coming back. Vanilla: 5 seconds. Only matters if something is actually healing you, so with PASSIVE HP REGEN at 0 you may not notice it.
parameters.logic: Higher = HP regen waits longer after you get hurt; lower = it starts sooner.
parameters.interaction: Only matters while PASSIVE HP REGEN or another heal-over-time effect is active.

parameters.label: Health Regen Strength
parameters.description: Scales health regeneration produced by compatible recovery effects. It does not create passive healing by itself: 100% keeps full effect strength, while lower values weaken that recovery.
parameters.rationale: How strong all health recovery over time is. Vanilla: Novice and Stalker 100%, Veteran 75%, Master 50%. Doesn't start healing by itself — it boosts or weakens healing that is already running.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps healing-over-time effects at full strength; lower weakens them, higher strengthens them.
parameters.interaction: PASSIVE HP REGEN is 0 in vanilla, so this matters mainly when another effect is already restoring health, such as low-health recovery.

parameters.label: Low-HP Recovery Rate
parameters.description: Controls the positive health-regeneration rate supplied by the normal low-health recovery effect. Vanilla uses 1.0; higher values recover health faster while the effect is active, and 0 disables this recovery contribution.
parameters.rationale: The small comeback heal the game gives you when you're almost dead. Vanilla: 1 HP/s. 0 removes it, so near-death means near-death; LOW HEALTH MECHANICS can cut it further.
parameters.interaction: HEALTH REGEN STRENGTH scales it, and LOW HEALTH MECHANICS can cut it further.

parameters.description: Turns on the extra low-health punishment used by vanilla Master.
parameters.rationale: Master's extra punishment for being badly hurt: your health barely recovers until you patch up. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran OFF, Master ON. The normal low-health system works either way.
parameters.logic: OFF = normal low-HP behaviour. ON = your health barely recovers while you're badly hurt.
parameters.interaction: It starts at the same HP as vanilla; LOW-HP RECOVERY RATE below sets how hard it bites.

parameters.logic: Higher = your health barely recovers while badly hurt; 0% removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Stacks on top of the normal low-HP recovery and HEALTH REGEN STRENGTH.

parameters.label: Max Stamina
parameters.description: Vanilla maximum stamina is 100. This changes the size of your stamina pool, not how fast it recovers or how much actions cost.
parameters.rationale: The size of your stamina bar. Vanilla: 100. A bigger bar lets you sprint, jump and swing longer before you're winded; recovery speed and action costs don't change.
parameters.interaction: Action costs stay fixed, so a bigger MAX STAMINA fits more actions into one bar.

notes: Runtime 2.0.5 Player.VitalParams.MaxSP = 100.

parameters.label: Sprint Stops Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, sprinting is disabled. Default: 16.1 of the vanilla 100 stamina pool.
parameters.rationale: When your stamina drops below this, you can't sprint any more until it recovers. Vanilla: 16.1 out of 100. Lower it to squeeze out a longer final dash.
parameters.logic: Higher = sprint locks out earlier; lower = you can sprint deeper into the bar.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with EXHAUSTION REGEN DELAY. Sprint speed and stamina drain are separate.

notes: The mapped threshold is the entry whose StateTags contains EStateTag::Sprint.

parameters.label: Exhaustion Regen Delay
parameters.description: Seconds before stamina regeneration resumes after sprint exhaustion.
parameters.rationale: How long you stand there gasping after sprinting yourself out before stamina starts coming back. Vanilla: 1 second.
parameters.logic: Higher = a longer pause before stamina refills after you run dry; lower = shorter.
parameters.interaction: Only after you run dry. SPRINT STOPS BELOW sets when sprint locks.

parameters.label: Boost Starts Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, the separate low-stamina recovery boost becomes eligible. Default: 30 stamina.
parameters.rationale: When stamina falls below this, the game gives you a short second-wind boost. Vanilla: 30 out of 100.
parameters.logic: Higher = the second wind kicks in sooner; lower = only when you're nearly empty.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with BOOST STRENGTH and BOOST DURATION. SPRINT STOPS BELOW is separate.

notes: The NormalSP boundary is 30; the LowSPThreshold branch starts at 0 and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints below that boundary.

parameters.label: Boost Strength
parameters.description: Regeneration strength of the temporary low-stamina recovery boost (10 stamina/s originally).
parameters.rationale: How strong that second wind is. Vanilla: 10 stamina/s on top of normal recovery. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher = a stronger second wind; lower = recovery stays close to normal.
parameters.interaction: BOOST STARTS BELOW sets its trigger; low-stamina BOOST DURATION sets how long it lasts.

parameters.label: Boost Duration
parameters.description: Seconds that the conditional low-stamina stamina regeneration boost remains active (4 seconds originally).
parameters.rationale: How long the second wind lasts once it kicks in. Vanilla: 4 seconds.
parameters.logic: Higher = the second wind lasts longer; lower = it ends sooner.
parameters.interaction: BOOST STARTS BELOW sets the trigger; BOOST STRENGTH sets how strong it is.

parameters.label: Speed-Limited Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while you are sprinting but your movement speed is being limited. The game decides when this slower sprint state is active.
parameters.rationale: Stamina drain when you hold sprint but something slows you down (heavy load, injury). Vanilla: −0.65, the same as normal running.
parameters.logic: More negative = it drains faster; 0 = no extra drain; positive = you recover while doing it.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with normal sprint stamina. Heavy load and other slowdowns decide when it kicks in.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in speed-limited sprint state

notes: CFG target is confirmed; exact runtime transition into EStateTag::SprintUnderRunSpeed is not fully documented.

parameters.label: Jogging-State Stamina Effect

parameters.rationale: Stamina effect while you jog (the game switches to it by itself; there's no key). Vanilla: 0 — no drain.
parameters.logic: Negative settings slow stamina recovery while jogging; 0 is neutral; positive settings help stamina recover.
parameters.interaction: Only jogging. Walking, running and sprinting have their own settings.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Jogging state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Jogging is confirmed; there is no separate player Jogging bind and exact activation semantics require runtime verification.

parameters.label: Slow-Run-State Stamina Effect

parameters.rationale: Stamina effect while you run slowly (the game switches to it by itself; there's no key). Vanilla: 0 — no drain.
parameters.logic: Negative = it costs stamina; 0 = neutral; positive = you recover while doing it. Not the Walk toggle.
parameters.interaction: Only slow running. Walking and jogging have their own settings.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal SlowRun state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::SlowRun is confirmed; SlowRunThreshold = 0.5 exists, but its complete state-selection semantics are not proven.

parameters.label: Vault Height
parameters.description: Changes the tallest obstacle you can vault over. The WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES markers are simple player-friendly height references.
parameters.rationale: The tallest obstacle you can climb over. Vanilla: 130 cm — the WAIST / EYES markers show what that means in-game. Raise it to vault fences and crates that used to block you.
parameters.logic: Higher = you can climb taller obstacles; lower = fewer things to climb. Jump distance doesn't change.
parameters.interaction: Only the height. Vault stamina cost is separate.

notes: The CFG field and vanilla value are confirmed from runtime 2.0.5.

parameters.label: Medium-Water Stamina Drain

parameters.logic: Higher = wading costs more stamina; lower = it's easier; 0 = free.
parameters.interaction: Only the drain. How deep the water must be stays vanilla.

parameters.label: Deep-Water Stamina Drain

parameters.description: Changes how quickly armor loses condition. Higher settings make armor last longer; lower settings make it wear out faster.
parameters.rationale: How long your armor holds up before it's falling apart. Vanilla: Novice 1.35×, Stalker 1×, Veteran 0.9×, Master 0.6×. Higher = fewer repair trips; protection itself doesn't change.
parameters.interaction: Only how fast armor wears. Protection, weapon wear and jamming are separate.

parameters.label: Ammo Weight
parameters.description: Scales ammunition weight while preserving the vanilla weight differences between ammo types.

notes: The current base CFG dump contains 34 concrete non-template ammo prototypes with non-zero effective Weight values.
Inherited ammo weights are resolved to their effective vanilla values and patched on the concrete child prototype so every ammo type follows the same multiplier.

parameters.rationale: How heavy ammo is in your backpack. Vanilla: 1×. 0× = weightless; 2× = double. Heavy calibers stay heavier than light ones.
parameters.interaction: Carry capacity and overload stay separate; only the ammo itself gets lighter or heavier.

parameters.label: Consumable Weight
parameters.description: Scales food and medicine item weight while preserving the vanilla differences between consumables.

notes: The current dump resolves 22 non-zero base-game Food/Medicine consumable prototypes plus the DLC1 MonolithDryRation.
Inherited consumable weights are patched on the concrete prototype so quest/special variants keep the same multiplier instead of depending on parent inheritance.

parameters.rationale: How heavy food and meds are in your backpack. Vanilla: 1×. 0× = weightless. Their effects don't change.
parameters.interaction: Effect strength and duration don't change. DLC1 dry rations are included when DLC1 is installed.

parameters.label: Weapon Weight

parameters.rationale: How heavy weapons are in your backpack. Vanilla: 1×. Lower it to carry a spare rifle without being slowed down; damage and handling don't change.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps vanilla weight. 0× makes them weightless; 2× doubles their weight.
parameters.interaction: Weapons keep their weight differences. MAXIMUM CARRY WEIGHT is separate.

parameters.rationale: How heavy suits and helmets are. Vanilla: 1×. Lower it to wear heavy armor without the weight penalty; protection doesn't change.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps vanilla weight. 0× makes them weightless; 2× doubles their weight.
parameters.interaction: Items keep their weight differences. Does not change maximum carry weight or any equipment protection statistics.

parameters.label: Global Anomaly Damage
parameters.description: This is the broad anomaly difficulty setting. It scales damaging anomaly output as a group while each anomaly keeps its own base damage value.
parameters.rationale: How much all damaging anomalies hurt, on top of each anomaly's own damage. Vanilla: Novice 0.3×, Stalker 1×, Veteran 1.45×, Master 1.75×. Your suit's protection still applies after this.
parameters.logic: Higher = every damaging anomaly hits harder; lower = softer. Each anomaly's own BASE still applies.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with each anomaly's own base damage, before armor and other protection.

parameters.label: Starvation Mechanics
parameters.description: Enables the extra starvation punishment bundle that vanilla Master adds on top of the normal hunger system. It is a discrete mechanics switch, not another hunger setting.
parameters.rationale: Master's starvation punishment once you're severely hungry: actions cost much more stamina, you lose health every few seconds and stop healing. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran OFF, Master ON. Normal hunger effects work either way.
parameters.logic: Once you're severely hungry: actions cost +200% stamina, you lose 4 HP every 10 s after a short delay, and health stops regenerating. OFF leaves only normal hunger.
parameters.interaction: Starvation still starts at the vanilla point. The controls below set drain, damage, interval, delay and health recovery.

parameters.label: Radiation Stamina Penalty
parameters.description: Enables the additional Master radiation penalty rather than changing radiation accumulation or radiation damage itself.
parameters.rationale: Master's extra stamina cost while you're heavily irradiated. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran OFF, Master ON. Radiation still builds up and hurts you either way.
parameters.logic: While you're heavily irradiated, actions cost extra stamina (+50% in vanilla). Normal radiation damage works either way.
parameters.interaction: It starts at the same radiation level as vanilla. RADIATION ACCUMULATION and RADIATION RECOVERY decide how fast you get there and back.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Mechanics
parameters.description: Enables the Master-only severe-fatigue penalty bundle. This is separate from ordinary sleepiness build-up, aiming-time penalties and reload penalties.
parameters.rationale: Master's punishment for being exhausted: smaller stamina bar, less carry capacity, more recoil, more sway and wider spread. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran OFF, Master ON. Normal tiredness effects work either way.
parameters.logic: Once you're severely tired: −20% max stamina, −20% carry weight, +55% recoil, more sway and wider spread (vanilla values). OFF leaves only normal tiredness.
parameters.interaction: Severe fatigue still starts at the vanilla point. The controls below set how hard each penalty hits.

parameters.label: Well-Fed Stamina Recovery Bonus
parameters.description: Changes the stamina-recovery bonus you get while well fed. Vanilla gives +20%.
parameters.rationale: Bonus stamina recovery while your stomach is full. Vanilla: +20% — a reward for eating before a fight. 0% removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher = a bigger stamina bonus for staying well fed; 0% removes it. It never turns into a penalty.
parameters.interaction: You stop being well fed at the vanilla point. STAMINA REGEN sets the normal recovery rate.

parameters.label: Starvation Action Cost
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina cost of actions while the Master starvation penalty is active. Vanilla adds +200%.
parameters.rationale: How much more stamina actions cost while you're starving under Master rules. Vanilla: +200% — three times the normal cost. 0% removes the extra. Only works while STARVATION MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: 100% means +100% extra stamina cost, not normal cost. 0% removes this extra starvation cost.
parameters.interaction: Only the extra cost per action. Severe hunger also slows stamina regen.

parameters.label: Starvation Damage
parameters.description: The Master starvation bundle applies a dedicated Hunger damage effect with a vanilla value of 4 per charge.
parameters.rationale: Health lost each time starvation hits under Master rules. Vanilla: 4 HP. 0 = starving no longer hurts directly. Only works while STARVATION MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Higher = each starvation hit takes more HP; 0 = no HP damage (the other penalties stay).
parameters.interaction: STARVATION DAMAGE INTERVAL controls how often the charge repeats, while STARVATION PENALTY DELAY controls when this effect begins after activation.

parameters.label: Starvation Damage Interval
parameters.description: Vanilla schedules the starvation damage charge every 10 seconds while the effect remains active.
parameters.rationale: Seconds between starvation hits. Vanilla: 10 seconds. Lower = the same damage comes faster. Only works while STARVATION MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Lower = the same damage comes more often; higher = it's spread out.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with STARVATION DAMAGE: together they set how fast starving hurts.

parameters.label: Starvation Penalty Delay
parameters.description: All three vanilla starvation penalties use a 3-second delay. This control keeps those delay values synchronized.
parameters.rationale: Grace period before the starvation penalties kick in. Vanilla: 3 seconds. Only works while STARVATION MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Lower = the penalties hit sooner once you're starving; higher = a longer grace period.
parameters.interaction: STARVATION MECHANICS turns the penalties on; this only sets the grace period before they start.

parameters.label: Starvation Health Recovery Penalty
parameters.description: Vanilla Master applies a 100% health-recovery penalty while the starvation bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much starving blocks your healing under Master rules. Vanilla: 100% — no healing at all. 0% removes it. Only works while STARVATION MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Higher = health recovers less while starving; 0% removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Cuts healing, not direct damage. Stacks with STARVATION DAMAGE and the Health regen settings.

parameters.label: Low Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: At the Low Sleepiness state, vanilla increases aiming time by 15%.
parameters.rationale: How much light tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +15% time to aim.
parameters.logic: Higher = aiming settles more slowly while slightly tired; 0 removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever you're slightly tired.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla raises the aiming-time penalty to +25% in the medium fatigue state.
parameters.rationale: How much moderate tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +25% time to aim.
parameters.logic: Higher = aiming is slower while moderately tired; 0 removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever you're moderately tired, instead of the low-fatigue aim delay.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla increases aiming time by +40% in the severe fatigue state.
parameters.rationale: How much severe tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +40% time to aim — sleep before a big fight.
parameters.logic: Higher = aiming is slower while severely tired; 0 removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever you're severely tired.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Reload Delay
parameters.description: Medium fatigue adds +15% to the reload-time effect in vanilla.
parameters.rationale: How much moderate tiredness slows your reloads. Vanilla: +15% reload time.
parameters.logic: Higher = slower reloads while moderately tired; 0 removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever you're moderately tired; the aim delay is separate.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Reload Delay
parameters.description: Controls how much severe fatigue slows your reloads. Vanilla severe fatigue adds 18.75% reload time.
parameters.rationale: How much severe tiredness slows your reloads. Vanilla: +18.75% reload time. Master fatigue can add more.
parameters.logic: Higher = slower reloads while severely tired; 0 removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever you're severely tired. SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS can add more on top.

parameters.label: Sleep HP Restore
parameters.description: Controls how much HP normal sleep restores when you wake up. Starts at 300 HP; adjustable from 0 to 600 HP.
parameters.rationale: How much health a full night's sleep gives back. Vanilla: 300 HP. 0 makes sleep stop healing you; up to 600 HP turns a night in a safe bed into a full patch-up.
parameters.logic: Higher = sleep heals more; 0 HP means sleep doesn't heal at all.
parameters.interaction: Medkits and passive HP regeneration remain separate.

parameters.label: Sleep Stamina Restore
parameters.description: Normal sleep restores stamina with a vanilla +100% Stamina effect.
parameters.rationale: How much stamina you wake up with after sleeping. Vanilla: a full bar (+100%).
parameters.interaction: Only the refill after sleep. Passive stamina regen and action costs are separate.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Stamina Loss
parameters.description: Vanilla Master reduces maximum stamina by 20% while its severe-fatigue bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much of your stamina bar you lose while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: 20%. 0% removes it. Only works while SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Higher = an even smaller stamina bar while severely tired; 0% removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: MAX STAMINA sets your normal bar; this loss only applies while you're severely tired.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Carry Loss
parameters.description: Vanilla Master applies a 20% loss to both the additional-inventory-weight and penalty-less-weight fatigue effects.
parameters.rationale: How much carry capacity you lose while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: 20%. 0% removes it. Only works while SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.logic: Higher = you can carry even less while severely tired; 0% removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Your normal carrying limit and equipment carry bonuses remain separate.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Recoil
parameters.description: Vanilla Master adds a +55% recoil effect while the severe-fatigue bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much harder your guns kick while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +55% recoil. 0% removes it. Only works while SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with other recoil. Reload and aim-time penalties are separate.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Aim Sway
parameters.description: Controls how much extra weapon sway Master severe fatigue adds while aiming.
parameters.rationale: How much more your sights wobble while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +40%. 0% removes it. Only works while SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.interaction: Recoil and shot spread are separate penalties of SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Shot Spread
parameters.description: Changes how much severe fatigue increases weapon spread.
parameters.rationale: How much wider your shots spread while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +50%. 0% removes it. Only works while SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS is ON.
parameters.interaction: Recoil and aim sway are separate penalties of SEVERE FATIGUE MECHANICS.

parameters.label: Master Radiation Stamina Cost Increase
parameters.description: When Master Radiation Mechanics is active at heavy radiation, this adds an extra stamina cost to stamina-consuming actions. Vanilla is +50%; 0% removes the extra stamina cost.

display.valueLabel: Extra stamina cost under heavy radiation

parameters.rationale: How much more stamina actions cost while heavily irradiated under Master rules. Vanilla: +50%. 0% removes it. Only works while RADIATION STAMINA PENALTY is ON.
parameters.logic: 50% means +50% extra stamina cost. 0% removes this extra radiation cost.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with the normal action costs. RADIATION ACCUMULATION sets how fast you get there.

parameters.label: Medium Bleeding Threshold
parameters.description: Sets when Medium bleeding begins.

notes: Runtime CFG threshold is 50 Bleeding points.
Medium bleeding also carries movement/no-sleep consequences.

parameters.rationale: Where on the bleeding meter a wound becomes a moderate bleed. Vanilla: 50.
parameters.logic: Keep MEDIUM below SEVERE. LOW bleeding still starts at the game's 0.1.
parameters.interaction: Sets only where the stage starts. Bleed damage is separate.

parameters.label: Severe Bleeding Threshold

notes: Runtime CFG threshold is 75 Bleeding points.

parameters.rationale: Where on the bleeding meter a wound becomes a severe bleed. Vanilla: 75.
parameters.logic: Keep SEVERE above MEDIUM. The Low threshold remains fixed at 0.1.
parameters.interaction: Sets only where the stage starts. Bleed damage is separate.

parameters.label: Low Bleeding Damage
parameters.description: Controls the health damage dealt by low bleeding each time its damage tick occurs. Vanilla uses 1 damage.
parameters.rationale: Health lost per tick from a light bleed. Vanilla: 1 HP.
parameters.interaction: Applies while you bleed lightly. NATURAL BLEEDING RECOVERY decides how long it lasts.

parameters.label: Medium Bleeding Damage
parameters.description: Controls the health damage dealt by medium bleeding each time its damage tick occurs. Vanilla uses 1.5 damage.
parameters.rationale: Health lost per tick from a moderate bleed. Vanilla: 1.5 HP.
parameters.interaction: Applies while you bleed moderately. Movement and sleep penalties are separate.

parameters.label: Severe Bleeding Damage
parameters.description: Controls the health damage dealt by severe bleeding each time its damage tick occurs. Vanilla uses 2 damage.
parameters.rationale: Health lost per tick from a severe bleed. Vanilla: 2 HP — that adds up fast without a bandage.
parameters.interaction: Applies while you bleed severely. BLEEDING SEVERITY changes how dangerous bleeding is overall.

parameters.label: Healing Item Efficiency Reduction
parameters.description: Turns on the extra consumable penalties used by vanilla Master. This includes the separate Bandage, Medkit and Army Medkit healing reductions shown below, plus a few food/energy-drink/artifact effects that are still bundled together.
parameters.rationale: Master's weaker meds: bandages and medkits heal less, plus a few food, energy-drink and artifact tweaks. Vanilla: Novice–Veteran OFF, Master ON. The healing cuts are the bars below.
parameters.logic: OFF = items work normally. ON = Master's weaker meds and item tweaks.
parameters.interaction: The healing controls below only matter while this is ON. A few food, energy-drink and Weird Kettle tweaks come with it and can't be set separately.

parameters.label: Damage by Anomaly

parameters.rationale: How hard electro anomalies hit you. Vanilla: 65 base damage, then scaled by GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE (Stalker 1×). Each anomaly type has its own bar on this board. 0 makes them harmless.
parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.

parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE. Only this anomaly type changes.

parameters.label: Fire Base Damage
parameters.description: Fine-tunes Fire damage without changing the other anomalies. Vanilla base damage is 60. Global Anomaly Damage still affects it too.
parameters.rationale: How hard fire anomalies hit you. Vanilla: 60 base damage, then scaled by GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE (Stalker 1×). 0 makes them harmless.
parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE. Only this anomaly type changes.

parameters.label: Carousel Base Damage
parameters.description: Fine-tunes Carousel damage without changing the other anomalies. Vanilla base damage is 105. Global Anomaly Damage still affects it too.
parameters.rationale: How hard carousel (gravity whirl) anomalies hit you. Vanilla: 105 base damage, then scaled by GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE (Stalker 1×). The hardest-hitting of the group. 0 makes them harmless.
parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE. Only this anomaly type changes.

parameters.label: Toxic Cloud Base Damage
parameters.description: Fine-tunes Toxic Cloud damage without changing the other anomalies. Vanilla base damage is 25. Global Anomaly Damage still affects it too.
parameters.rationale: How hard toxic cloud anomalies hit you. Vanilla: 25 base damage, then scaled by GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE (Stalker 1×). 0 makes them harmless.
parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE. Only this anomaly type changes.

parameters.label: Steam Base Damage
parameters.description: Fine-tunes Steam damage without changing the other anomalies. Vanilla base damage is 60. Global Anomaly Damage still affects it too.
parameters.rationale: How hard steam anomalies hit you. Vanilla: 60 base damage, then scaled by GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE (Stalker 1×). 0 makes them harmless.
parameters.logic: Higher = this anomaly hits harder; 0 makes it harmless. EFFECTIVE = BASE × GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE, before your protection.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies with GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE. Only this anomaly type changes.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Movement Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal movement speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores FlycatcherVelocityChange as -50%. The UI exposes retained movement speed instead: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: How fast you can still move when a Flycatcher grabs you. Vanilla: 50% of normal speed. 100% = no slowdown; 0% = stuck in place.
parameters.logic: Higher = you move more freely inside it; 100% = no slowdown; 0% = stuck in place.
parameters.interaction: Only your walking speed inside. FLYCATCHER TURN SPEED, bullet slowdown and regen penalties are separate.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Turn Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal look/turn speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores both yaw and pitch effects as -0.7. One UI value intentionally drives both targets: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: How fast you can still turn and look around inside a Flycatcher. Vanilla: 30% of normal. 100% = no slowdown.
parameters.logic: Higher = you turn more freely inside it; 100% = no slowdown; 0% = you can't turn.
parameters.interaction: Only turning, both sideways and up/down. FLYCATCHER MOVEMENT SPEED is separate.

parameters.label: Clicker Health Damage
parameters.description: Controls the direct health damage dealt by a Clicker hit without changing the anomaly's equipment corrosion or behavior.
parameters.rationale: How much health a Clicker hit takes. Vanilla: 70 base damage. Only the health damage changes; the hit still wears down your gear as usual.
parameters.logic: Higher = each Clicker burn hurts more, before difficulty and your protection; 0 removes this health damage.
parameters.interaction: Only the Clicker's hit damage changes. GLOBAL ANOMALY DAMAGE and your protection still apply; its gear corrosion is untouched.

parameters.label: Glass Shards Health Damage
parameters.description: Scales Glass Shards health damage at both movement-speed tiers while preserving the stronger high-speed hit.

notes: Runtime CFG stores low-speed Glass Shards damage as 20-25 and high-speed damage as 100. The slider scales both tiers together and leaves MinSpeed/MaxSpeed thresholds unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How much health Glass Shards take as you move through them. Vanilla: 1×. Running through still hurts more than walking.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps vanilla Glass Shards damage; 0× removes its health damage; 2× doubles both walking and running damage.
parameters.interaction: GLASS SHARDS BLEEDING and Glass Shards equipment corrosion remain separate effects. This control does not change the anomaly speed thresholds.

parameters.label: Glass Shards Bleeding
parameters.description: Scales Glass Shards bleeding at both movement-speed tiers while preserving the stronger high-speed bleeding effect.

notes: Runtime CFG stores Glass Shards bleeding as 20 at the low-speed tier and 60 at the high-speed tier. The slider scales both values together.

parameters.rationale: How badly Glass Shards make you bleed. Vanilla: 1×. 0× = no bleeding; running through still cuts deeper than walking.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps vanilla Glass Shards bleeding; 0× removes it; 2× doubles it.
parameters.interaction: GLASS SHARDS HEALTH DAMAGE is separate; how fast you must move and gear corrosion stay vanilla.

parameters.label: Soap Bubble Health Damage
parameters.description: Controls the direct Chemical Burn health damage of the Soap Bubble anomaly.

notes: Runtime CFG stores SoapBubbleDamage ValueMin/ValueMax as 100/100. Particle and other Soap Bubble behavior is intentionally left untouched.

parameters.rationale: How much health a Soap Bubble's chemical burn takes. Vanilla: 100. 0 removes the health damage only.
parameters.logic: Higher = Soap Bubble hurts more; 0 removes its health damage.
parameters.interaction: Only the damage. How the Soap Bubble moves and spreads stays vanilla.

parameters.label: Fireball Health Damage
parameters.description: Controls the direct Burn health damage of the Fireball anomaly.

notes: Runtime CFG stores FireBallAnomaly ValueMin/ValueMax as 100/100 Burn damage. Fireball movement/trail behavior remains untouched.

parameters.rationale: How much health a Fireball's burn takes. Vanilla: 100. 0 removes the health damage only.
parameters.logic: Higher = Fireball hurts more; 0 removes its health damage.
parameters.interaction: Only the damage. How the Fireball moves stays vanilla.

parameters.label: Diamond Health Damage
parameters.description: Controls the direct Strike health damage applied by the Diamond anomaly.

notes: CFG prototype confirmed, but DiamondAnomaly has no independently confirmed in-game encounter or spawn; not shown in the TCD UI, preserved for legacy preset compatibility.
Runtime CFG stores DiamondDPS ValueMin/ValueMax as 15/15.

parameters.rationale: How much health a Diamond hit takes. Vanilla: 15. Its bleeding is a separate setting.
parameters.logic: Higher = Diamond hurts more; 0 removes its health damage.
parameters.interaction: DIAMOND BLEEDING is controlled separately.

parameters.label: Diamond Bleeding
parameters.description: Controls the bleeding effect applied by the Diamond anomaly.

notes: CFG prototype confirmed, but DiamondAnomaly has no independently confirmed in-game encounter or spawn; not shown in the TCD UI, preserved for legacy preset compatibility.
Runtime CFG stores DiamondBleeding ValueMin/ValueMax as 10/10.

parameters.rationale: How badly a Diamond hit makes you bleed. Vanilla: 10 bleed pts. 0 = no bleeding from it.
parameters.logic: Higher = Diamond cuts make you bleed more; 0 = no bleeding.
parameters.interaction: DIAMOND HEALTH DAMAGE is a separate setting.

parameters.label: Psy Drain Strength
parameters.description: Scales the Psy anomaly's continuous negative Psy-point effect without changing its other behavior.

notes: Runtime CFG stores PsyAnomalyIncreaseRegen as DegenPsyPoints with ValueMin/ValueMax = -1.7/-1.7. The UI exposes the magnitude as a positive 0-200% multiplier.

parameters.rationale: How fast psy anomalies drain your psy meter. Vanilla: 1×. 0× = they stop draining it; 2× = twice as fast.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps vanilla psy drain; 0× removes it; 2× doubles it.
parameters.interaction: Only the constant Psy drain. Other Psy effects stay vanilla.

parameters.label: Artifact Spawn Chance
parameters.description: Scales the chance that a spawn attempt in an anomaly field produces an artifact: SpawnChanceBase 25% and SpawnChanceBonus 15%, each capped at 100%.

notes: The world's anomaly-field artifacts come from UniversalArtifactSpawner (73 world spawn points) and its short-range child LesserZoneMagneticShortDistance. Quest and unique spawners (Weird*, Quest*, Water Drip) are not touched.
Values apply to all four zone ranks (Newbie, Experienced, Veteran, Master areas) and do not depend on the selected difficulty.
SpawnChanceBase (25) and SpawnChanceBonus (15) are both scaled; how the engine applies the bonus is not documented, so both keep their ratio.

parameters.rationale: Odds that a field actually drops an artifact when it regrows. Vanilla: 1× (25% + 15% bonus). 2× = 50% (+30%); 0× = anomaly fields never grow artifacts.
parameters.logic: 1× keeps the game's 25% / 15%. Each value is multiplied and capped at 100%. 0× removes world anomaly artifacts; quest and unique artifacts stay.
parameters.interaction: RARE LUCK and PER SPAWN shape what you find. Fields still refill on the game's own schedule (after emissions).

parameters.label: Rare Artifact Luck
parameters.description: Multiplies the Rare and Epic share of the artifact rarity split in every zone rank and renormalises Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic back to 100%.

notes: The world's anomaly-field artifacts come from UniversalArtifactSpawner (73 world spawn points) and its short-range child LesserZoneMagneticShortDistance. Quest and unique spawners (Weird*, Quest*, Water Drip) are not touched.
Values apply to all four zone ranks (Newbie, Experienced, Veteran, Master areas) and do not depend on the selected difficulty.
Vanilla split (Common/Uncommon/Rare/Epic): Newbie 80/20/0/0, Experienced 50/48/1.9/0.1, Veteran 30/59/10/1, Master 10/65/20/5. Newbie areas have no rare artifacts and stay unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How often a find is rare or epic. Vanilla: 1× (25% in Master zones, 11% in Veteran). 2× roughly doubles that; 0.5× makes a top-tier artifact a real event. Newbie zones never drop rare ones.
parameters.logic: Higher = more Rare and Epic artifacts, fewer common ones. Newbie areas never grow rare artifacts, and still don't.
parameters.interaction: Only the rarity. ARTIFACT SPAWN CHANCE and PER SPAWN set how many appear.

parameters.label: Artifacts per Spawn
parameters.description: Sets the spawners' Count: how many artifacts a successful spawn in an anomaly field creates (vanilla 1).

notes: The world's anomaly-field artifacts come from UniversalArtifactSpawner (73 world spawn points) and its short-range child LesserZoneMagneticShortDistance. Quest and unique spawners (Weird*, Quest*, Water Drip) are not touched.
Values apply to all four zone ranks (Newbie, Experienced, Veteran, Master areas) and do not depend on the selected difficulty.
Count is 1 in every world spawner; whether the engine places several artifacts per spawn needs an in-game check.

parameters.rationale: How many artifacts drop at once when a field spawns. Vanilla: 1. 2–3 turn a well-searched field into a jackpot.
parameters.logic: 1 = vanilla, one artifact per spawn; 2 or 3 = that many.
parameters.interaction: Multiplies every artifact that spawns; SPAWN CHANCE decides how often that happens.

parameters.label: Mutant Part Drop Chances
parameters.description: Changes mutant-part drop chances by mutant family.

notes: Runtime CFG explicitly stores Chance = 0.15 and Count = 1 for BlinddogLootGenerator.

parameters.rationale: Chance a dead blind dog leaves one part you can sell or use. Vanilla: 15% — most kills give nothing. Doesn't change how many blind dogs spawn.
parameters.interaction: Only this mutant's drop chance. Other mutants keep their own.
